rationale:
Evidence from iteration 3 (kd 0.30, base_speed 1.4, sensors at ±0.05 m, sensor_size 0.012, last_direction): score 53.94, the best so far. Oval progress rose to 0.124 with 0 line-loss events, but max_error was 0.0609, still just over the 0.06 m off-track limit. S-bend progress was 0.1575 with 1 line-loss event, and slalom progress was 0.1075 with 1 line-loss event. Slalom is marginally below the iteration 1 value (0.110), and s-bend and slalom still lose the line once each run.

The Evaluator's rules apply in two places. Rule (b): the oval has max_error at or above 0.06 with 0 line losses, so the sensor footprint should be tested before changing speed again. Rule (c): line_loss_events stays at 1 on s-bend, so the recovery direction should change from last_direction.

Changes: (1) sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016, so a wider footprint keeps the 25 mm tape in view on the first corner and may lower the oval max_error. (2) controller.line_loss last_direction to search_right (signal fixed at +1, steering left), which the Evaluator named as an option for recovering the line on s-bend and slalom. (3) base_speed stays at 1.4 and kd stays at 0.30, since iteration 3 gave the best score and the slalom shortfall is small. Sensor positions (±0.05 m, 5 sensors), weights, kp 4.0, ki 0.05 and the other geometry are unchanged.

Risk: two fields change at once (footprint and line-loss direction). If the score falls, the cause could be either one. The footprint is most likely to affect the oval; the line-loss direction most likely affects s-bend and slalom. Expected result: oval max_error below 0.06 with 0 line losses, s-bend and slalom line-loss events reduced to 0 or kept at 1 with a different outcome, and progress at or above iteration 3 values (oval 0.124, s-bend 0.1575, slalom 0.1075). If s-bend or slalom line-loss events go up, the search direction was wrong: next try search_left with the same geometry.
